battery.title: Battery and sensors
battery.description: The battery, the power sensors the learned planner reads, and the solar forecast. Changing a sensor restarts the integration (as an HA restart would).

data.load_power_entity: House load power sensor (inverter AC output)

data_description.battery_soc_entity: Available battery energy in kWh. The classic planner reads it; the learned planner uses it only when no gauge sensor is set.
data_description.gauge_entity: The percent the inverter itself reports. Leave empty to derive it from the battery SOC sensor and the capacity.
data_description.load_power_entity: Needed for learning. Power the inverter delivers to the house.
data_description.grid_power_entity: Needed for learning. Power the inverter takes from the grid.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Optional. Solar power into the inverter.
data_description.solar_forecast_entity: Solcast-shaped forecast with hourly detail (detailedHourly or detailedForecast).
data_description.solar_forecast_tomorrow_entity: Optional. Guessed from today's forecast sensor when empty.
data_description.solar_actual_entity: Sensor reporting cumulative solar production today in kWh (enables forecast accuracy tracking). Optional.
data_description.battery_capacity: Total usable capacity of your battery system.
data_description.base_load_kw: Average house draw. The classic planner's starting point, and the learned planner's load until it has history.

tariff.title: Tariff
tariff.description: When electricity costs what. The planner works with three periods on a TOU day: off-peak (cheap), mid-peak (middle) and peak (dear), mid-peak running straight into peak. A season can change the hours and prices for some months. Holidays are off-peak all day. Changing an hour restarts the integration; prices and holidays take effect within a minute. The defaults are PGE Time of Day.

data_description.midpeak_start_hour: When mid-peak rates begin. Set it to the peak start hour if your plan has no mid-peak (two prices only).
data_description.peak_start_hour: When the most expensive rates begin.
data_description.peak_end_hour: When peak rates end and off-peak resumes.
data_description.weekdays_only: On: the mid-peak and peak windows apply Monday to Friday only, weekends are off-peak all day. Off: every day.
data_description.offpeak_price: Optional, per kWh. Shown on the Learned Plan sensor; the daily cost counts mid-peak and peak only.
data_description.midpeak_price: Per kWh in the mid-peak window. The daily message's dollars use it.
data_description.peak_price: Per kWh in the peak window. It must not be below the mid-peak price: the planner tops up in mid-peak so as not to buy at peak.
data_description.tariff_seasons: Optional. One season per line: months, a colon, then periods with hours, a price or both, for example: Summer 06-09: mid-peak 7-15, peak 15-20 0.52. Months in no season use the hours and prices above. Hours replace the day's windows (give peak; mid-peak must end where peak starts); a season with prices only keeps the hours above.
data_description.holiday_preset: Days your utility prices off-peak all day: no charge the night before for them, no weekly top-up the evening before a mid-week one, nothing graded or learned as a weekday. Choosing a preset fills the rules below with its own when you save; editing the rules makes it Custom. PGE: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas. US federal: the eleven federal holidays. Both move a Saturday holiday to Friday and a Sunday one to Monday. None: no holidays.
data_description.holiday_rules: One rule per line, an optional name after it: 01-01 is a date, 11-thu-4 the fourth Thursday of November, 05-mon-last the last Monday of May; sat->fri, sun->mon moves a date that falls on a weekend.
data_description.holiday_dates: Optional. Single days that are off-peak all day, for example 2026-12-24 Christmas Eve, one per line. Kept whatever the preset.

learned.title: Learned planner
learned.description: Which planner controls the inverter, and how cautious the learned one is. The planner, peak margin, load quantile, solar confidence and gauge floor are also settings on the device page.

data.full_charge_months: Months that charge to full every TOU night
data.load_quantile: Plan for this share of days (load quantile)
data.solar_confidence: Share of forecast solar to count on
data.gauge_floor_pct: Gauge reading at which the inverter hands over to grid
data.peak_margin_kwh: Reserve to keep above the handover at peak end
data.handover_recovery_pct: Gauge the inverter recharges to after a handover
data.stale_minutes: Minutes without change that mean the battery data is frozen

data_description.planner: classic: the original planner controls the inverter and the learned planner only reports. learned: the learned planner controls the inverter. Also on the device page as the Planner select.
data_description.load_quantile: 0.8 means the plan covers the load of 8 days out of 10. Also on the device page; a change there takes effect within a minute.
data_description.solar_confidence: 0.7 means only 70 percent of the forecast is relied on. Also on the device page; a change there takes effect within a minute.
data_description.gauge_floor_pct: Where the inverter's own SOC Low setting hands the house to the grid. The learned planner plans energy above this. Also on the device page; a change there takes effect within a minute.
data_description.peak_margin_kwh: The learned planner tops up in mid-peak if the battery would end peak with less than this above the handover. Also on the device page; a change there takes effect within a minute.
data_description.handover_recovery_pct: After handing the house to the grid at the floor, the inverter grid-charges its battery back to this level and stays on grid. The learned planner counts that charge as a cost of running out in peak.
data_description.stale_minutes: If neither the gauge nor any power sensor changes for this long while power is flowing, the readings count as missing: no learning, safe fallbacks, one alert. An idle system (every power sensor at zero) is not frozen. 0 turns the check off.

packs.title: Third-party packs
packs.description: Optional capacity tracking for battery packs the inverter does not manage. Adding or removing a pack restarts the integration.

data.pack_current_charge_positive: Pack current is positive when charging
data.pack_capacity_ah: Rated capacity of each third-party pack

data_description.pack_current_entities: Optional. One current sensor per pack the inverter does not manage. Adds a charge estimate (amp-hours from the last full charge) and a capacity trend sensor per pack. Voltage and percent sensors of the same pack are found by name (..._voltage, ..._battery).
data_description.pack_current_charge_positive: Turn off if the pack reports discharge as a positive current.
data_description.bus_voltage_entity: Optional. Empty: the mean of the packs' own voltage sensors.
data_description.pack_capacity_ah: Used to turn amp-hours since full into a percent.
data_description.capacity_v_high: Each discharge from full is measured from where the bus falls through this voltage.
data_description.capacity_v_low: ... to where it falls through this one. Pick two that most deep evenings reach.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Where the daily report and alerts go.

data_description.notifications_enabled: Daily report, review notice, and alerts (frozen data, inverter not responding).
data_description.notify_entity: A notify service, for example notify.mobile_app_yourphone. Empty: no notifications.
data_description.verbose_logging: Write the classic planner's simulation table to the log at warning level.

classic.title: Classic planner (legacy)
classic.description: Settings only the classic planner uses. It is kept for comparison and as a fallback; new features go into the learned planner.

data_description.min_safe_soc_kwh: The classic planner's floor; it plans never to go below this.
data_description.charge_threshold: The classic planner ignores a charge smaller than this.
data_description.schedule_hours: Hours the classic planner calculates the night charge, comma-separated, for example 3,4,5,6.
data_description.seasonal_preservation: Classic planner only: after peak in the hold months, hold the battery and run the house from the grid. The learned planner decides holds itself.

error.invalid_voltage_range: The lower voltage must be below the upper voltage.
error.invalid_time_range: Rate periods must be in order: mid-peak start, then peak start (the same hour means no mid-peak), then peak end.
